items.note: Twelve-week classroom experiment with 120 animation students split into GAI-supported and conventional teaching; outcomes are pre/post learning, knowledge application, motivation, and satisfaction, and creativity is claimed but no creativity score on student output is described.

College freshmen in experimental and control groups brainstormed for descriptive writing, the experimental group with GenAI text-to-video clips; idea assessments show more ideas in less time (fluency); N and allocation not in the abstract, which was read from a search summary of the Springer page.

Natural experiment around GitHub Copilot's 2021 launch (Python supported, R not) on open-source contributions, classified as substantive (new functionality) versus incremental; Copilot raised contributions 28 to 40 percent, more for incremental work; no individual participants assigned; SSRN version 10.2139/ssrn.4684662 is the same work.

Two within-subjects studies (N = 21) of AToM CoWriter, a proactive creative-writing assistant that infers cognitive writing processes, versus comparison configurations; reports better expressiveness and idea exploration, but whether these are scored on output or self-reported is unclear; below 50 participants.

Within-subjects study with 14 designers comparing the Surprise2Refine axis-centered agent design tool with a comparison workflow; 'perceived creativity of design outcomes' may be self-rated; below 50 participants; ACM version doi 10.1145/3830398.3830612.

Twelve-week quasi-experiment with 118 design students: a value-sensitive custom generative-AI pipeline (LoRA, ControlNet) versus traditional methods for heritage design; outcomes are aesthetic appreciation, design implementation, and cultural identity, with no explicit creativity score on outputs.

Uses quasi-experimental data to relate cognitive, informative, and logical dimensions of human-AI interaction to the novelty and usefulness of creative outputs by skill level; associational analysis among AI users, and whether a no-AI or alternative-AI arm exists is not stated.

Study with 70 third-year Chinese university students in which an experimental group used the KITS AI tool for choral arrangement; creative skills measured with the Creative Skills Assessment Scale and an arrangement-skills method; abstract read from a search summary of the ScienceDirect page (paywalled), and whether the scale scores student output is unclear.

Pre/post quasi-experiment with 85 digital-media students in intact classes assigned to GAI-assisted or traditional advertising design instruction; design work scored on five dimensions including creativity (largest effect, ANCOVA).

Mixed-method experiment with 160 novice designers across four AI-support conditions (text-to-image tools, unstructured versus scaffolded use); expert-rated quality and originality plus similarity metrics for visual diversity; unstructured use gave more polish but lower originality and diversity; SSRN title has a stray comma.
